decision: Choose the next action after all Day 12 SFT checkpoints failed the Base-relative math guardrail.

recommended_course_route.action: Close Day 12 as an informative negative result, keep frozen test unconsumed, complete Day 13 reading, and carry the optimizer hypothesis into Day 16.
recommended_course_route.reason: This preserves the preregistered experiment and avoids spending GPU time on an unplanned rescue run that cannot support a clean causal claim.

recommended_recovery_route.name: Day12b recovery
recommended_recovery_route.principle: Diagnose cheaply, repair the dominant data-format failure, then add retention controls one at a time.

promotion_gate.frozen_test_access: Only after one checkpoint passes all dev gates

options.change: No training. Re-evaluate only A-25/B-25 math with an explicit step-by-step math instruction and a controlled stopping variant; retain the original protocol as the selection result.
options.tests: Whether reasoning is still latent and the observed regression is mainly task routing / premature EOS rather than erased capability.
options.decision_rule: If math materially recovers, prioritize prompt/data routing. If it does not, prioritize capability retention and data quality.

options.change: Keep Base, seed, token budget, optimizer and source pool fixed. Add task-specific routing and remove the globally reusable FinQA Calculation template; save 5/10/15/25% checkpoints.
options.tests: The highest-confidence diagnosis: finance answer-format leakage into GSM8K.
options.decision_rule: Stop at 25% unless math reaches at least 10/28 while code reaches at least 5/28.

options.change: Using the repaired data only, compare the current constant 2e-5 schedule with one conservative schedule such as 1e-5 plus cosine decay; keep full-parameter training for this comparison.
options.tests: Whether continued constant-peak updates are causing avoidable Base-capability drift.
options.decision_rule: Prefer the conservative schedule only if it improves the guardrail frontier, not merely train loss.

options.change: After the data and LR questions are resolved, compare full fine-tuning with LoRA or add a small Base/replay or KL anchor.
options.tests: Whether parameter-efficient updates or an explicit reference constraint reduce catastrophic interference in the 0.6B model.
options.causal_clarity: medium unless LoRA and anchoring are tested separately
options.decision_rule: Adopt only if code gains remain while math and aggregate gates pass.

options.change: First evaluate an instruction-tuned checkpoint as a new baseline; if the goal is utility rather than the Base-to-SFT lesson, fine-tune that checkpoint with LoRA and repaired task routing, or move to a larger model.
options.tests: Whether the 0.6B Base starting point is the limiting product choice rather than the specific Day 12 recipe.
options.causal_clarity: low as a Day 12 ablation, high practical relevance
options.decision_rule: Treat this as a new experiment family with a fresh baseline and gates; do not compare it as if only the mixture changed.

not_recommended: Continue A or B beyond 100% with the same constant-LR full-parameter recipe.
Change data format, LR, model, LoRA and mixture in one run if the goal is to learn which mechanism mattered.
Select B-25 only because it has the best code score; it still fails the math guardrail and aggregate Base baseline.
Consume the frozen test before a dev-eligible checkpoint exists.
confidence: Share with caveats: the ordering is evidence-based, but expected recovery is unverified until the proposed controlled runs are executed.
